name: market_knowledge
description: Curated educational knowledge dataset shipped with NEEZY. Reference material for the local chat assistant: indicator definitions, candle patterns, risk rules, and Deriv public API notes. Educational only; not financial advice.

indicators.name: EMA
indicators.definition: Exponential moving average; weights recent closes more than a simple average.
indicators.reading: Price above a rising 50 EMA is bullish context; a 9/21 cross marks short-term momentum shifts.

indicators.name: RSI
indicators.definition: Relative Strength Index, 0-100 oscillator of average gains versus losses.
indicators.reading: Above 70 overbought, below 30 oversold; 50 is the mid-line. Hidden divergence signals weakening momentum.
indicators.caveat: Can stay extreme in strong trends.

indicators.name: MACD
indicators.definition: Difference of two EMAs plus a signal EMA of that difference (histogram).
indicators.reading: Histogram crossing zero agrees with trend change; shrinking histogram warns of momentum loss.

indicators.name: ATR
indicators.definition: Average True Range; mean candle range including gaps.
indicators.reading: Rising ATR means wider stops and bigger targets; falling ATR means compression.

indicators.name: Bollinger
indicators.reading: Squeeze (narrow bands) often precedes expansion; rides on the band mark strong trends.
indicators.caveat: Bands are not support/resistance by themselves.

indicators.name: Supertrend
indicators.definition: ATR trailing band that flips sides when price closes through it.
indicators.reading: Direction of the line is the regime; bars-since-flip shows how fresh the regime is.

indicators.name: Stochastic
indicators.definition: Close position within the recent high-low range, smoothed.
indicators.reading: Crosses under 80 / over 20 mark turning attempts; works best with trend filter.

indicators.name: ADX
indicators.definition: Average Directional Index; strength of trend regardless of direction.
indicators.reading: Above 25 suggests a trending market; below 20 suggests range conditions.

indicators.name: Keltner
indicators.reading: Close outside the channel with rising ATR marks expansion; inside means compression.
indicators.caveat: Channel width depends on ATR settings.

indicators.name: Donchian
indicators.definition: Highest high and lowest low over the lookback window.
indicators.reading: Break of the upper channel is a classic breakout signal; width shows volatility.

indicators.name: CCI
indicators.definition: Commodity Channel Index; deviation of price from its average.
indicators.reading: Beyond +100 / -100 marks strong momentum in that direction.

indicators.name: Stochastic RSI
indicators.definition: Stochastic applied to RSI instead of price.
indicators.reading: Faster than RSI alone; crosses near extremes flag early turns.
indicators.caveat: Very noisy; use with a trend filter.

patterns.name: Bullish engulfing
patterns.definition: A down candle fully engulfed by the next up candle.
patterns.context: Most meaningful after a decline at a support level.

patterns.name: Bearish engulfing
patterns.definition: An up candle fully engulfed by the next down candle.
patterns.context: Most meaningful after a rally at resistance.

patterns.name: Hammer
patterns.definition: Small body near the high with a long lower wick.
patterns.context: Shows rejection of lower prices after a fall.

patterns.name: Shooting star
patterns.definition: Small body near the low with a long upper wick.
patterns.context: Shows rejection of higher prices after a rise.

patterns.name: Doji
patterns.context: Signals balance; wait for the confirming candle.

patterns.name: Inside bar
patterns.definition: Candle range entirely inside the prior candle's range.
patterns.context: Compression; breakout of the mother bar often follows.

risk_rules: Define the maximum loss per idea in R before entering; 1R is the amount risked.
Position size from stop distance: size = risk_amount / (stop_distance * value_per_unit).
ATR-based stops (1.5-2 ATR) adapt to volatility better than fixed pip stops.
Reward-to-risk above 1.5 lets a sub-50% hit rate still be positive expectancy.
Expectancy = (win_rate * avg_win) - (loss_rate * avg_loss); track it in R.
A streak of losses is expected; judge a rule on a sample of trades, not one.
Backtest results are simulations with charged spread; out-of-sample verdicts are not forecasts.
Never risk money needed elsewhere; educational tools do not manage your account.

glossary.candle: One OHLC record for a fixed interval (epoch, open, high, low, close).
glossary.granularity: Candle interval in seconds; NEEZY supports Deriv's standard granularities (60-3600).
glossary.divergence: Price makes a new extreme while the oscillator does not; momentum is fading.
glossary.drawdown: Peak-to-trough decline of an equity curve.
glossary.edge: Positive expectancy verified out of sample; the label NEEZY's study engine assigns cautiously.
glossary.out-of-sample: Data held back from parameter selection, used only to validate.
glossary.spread: Difference between buy and sell price; charged by the simulation on every trade.
glossary.t-stat: Ratio of an estimate to its standard error; NEEZY wants 2 or more before calling an edge.
glossary.volatility: Standard deviation of returns; drives ATR, band width, and stop size.
glossary.WAL mode: SQLite journal mode that allows concurrent readers with one writer; used by NEEZY's local DB.

deriv_api.auth: Public market data only; no token needed for these calls.

calls.contracts_for: Available contract types per symbol: {contracts_for: SYMBOL, currency: 'USD'}.
